{#fsho} # Introduction

{#uiub} Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, with a high prevalence in Asia [@w:w1]. The outcome of patients with T4 esophageal cancer, defined as a tumor that invades neighboring structures (e.g., aorta, trachea, bronchus, and lung), is extremely poor [@w:w2]. Despite advances in surgical treatment, these tumors are usually considered inoperable; however, surgery alone has not improved the prognosis of patients with T4 esophageal tumors [@w:w3].

{#i30u} Two distinct therapeutic options are currently available for T4 esophageal cancers: chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery (CRT-S), which comprises esophagectomy following downstaging of the tumor by CRT, and definitive chemoradiotherapy (D-CRT), which is designed to avoid esophagectomy by using maximum doses of irradiation [@w:w4]. Until now, D-CRT has been the standard alternative curative management for patients with locally advanced disease who are not eligible for or refuse surgery . To our knowledge, there is little information on the differences in the clinical outcomes of patients with T4 ESCC who undergo D-CRT and those who receive CRT-S. In this study, we discuss these two treatment modalities.

ops.markdown: We next examined the pattern of first failure, classifying each event as local, regional nodal, or distant. In previous studies of locally advanced esophageal cancer treated with chemoradiation followed by esophagectomy, local failure occurred in 4.5–67% of patients, regional nodal failure in 10–57.9%, and distant failure in 21–32% [@w:w15]. Local failure was associated with fewer lymph nodes (LNs) examined and with close or positive margins; regional nodal failure with fewer LNs examined and a larger pretreatment tumor size; and distant recurrence with a higher pathologic nodal stage, ulceration, perineural invasion, residual disease, and a higher post-treatment PET SUV max. Patients who achieved a pathologic complete response were less likely to develop distant recurrence [@w:w16]. In our study, all cases were evaluated as downstaged to operable disease by CT, endoscopy, and upper gastrointestinal contrast study. Distant metastasis predominated in the CRT-S group (8/32, 25.0%), whereas the local progression rate was only 3.1% (1/32); this low rate may be partially related to the high pathological complete response (pCR) rate (37.5%, 12/32), the limited nodal burden (N0, 23/32; N1, 3/32; N2, 4/32; N3, 0/32), the high negative margin rate (32/32, 100%), and the high R0 resection rate (30/32, 93.75%) [@w:w17].
